source.quote: This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`.

tasks.reasoning: The repo uses the Python anthropic SDK with only a lower bound (>=0.40.0 in requirements.txt). The provider notes say the new SDK majors (Python v1.0 exists) send API version 2026-10-21 by default. Any fresh install or CI build may therefore silently move every call to the new API version. The repo does not call POST /v1/messages directly; it uses beta agents, sessions, files, skills and environments. So the documented Messages breakages (sampling params, document/citation placement) do not apply directly. What is uncertain is whether the beta managed-agents endpoints or the Python SDK 1.x surface (method names, removed parameters, betas handling) changed. The migration agent should either pin anthropic<1.0 in requirements.txt, or check the Python SDK 1.0 changelog and migration guide against every beta.* call site and pin to a verified version.

## New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01 [Needs review]

### Change

Raised the anthropic floor in requirements.txt from >=0.40.0 to >=1.0.0. This makes every install send anthropic-version 2026-10-21. I added tests/test_anthropic_version.py. It runs with `python3 tests/test_anthropic_version.py` and is registered as a check. No application code changed.

Files touched:
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_anthropic_version.py`

### Why

Older SDKs send 2023-06-01 and a loose floor lets installs vary. The repo makes no POST /v1/messages calls, so the Messages breakages (sampling params, document/citation placement) don't apply. I confirmed that every beta.* method used exists in SDK 2.4.0. I also confirmed the SDK's default anthropic-version header is 2026-10-21.

> This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`.

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anthropic-version-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- anthropic-version-proof, added by the agent: `python3 tests/test_anthropic_version.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Behaviour of the beta managed-agents endpoints (agents, sessions, environments, skills) at 2026-10-21 was not confirmed. Only the method surface was checked, not response shapes.
- The test sends only files.list and skills.list through a mock transport. The other beta calls are only checked to exist.
- No migration guide for the beta endpoints was read.
- The baseline failure of the proof check is just the missing test file. It doesn't show that the old code sent 2023-06-01.
- Model claude-opus-4-7 was left unchanged and its validity was not checked.
- No lockfile exists and no other test suite exists.
- The agent wrote no test of this change and gave no reason why none can be written.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- All API calls now go out with anthropic-version 2026-10-21 (SDK default), where before the version depended on the installed SDK.
- The SDK floor is now 1.0.0. The newest 2.x release installs on a fresh install and needs httpx2.

---

review.summary: The PR only raises the SDK floor to anthropic>=1.0.0 and adds a header test; no call site changes. The quoted guide says it 'lists the code changes' for moving from 2023-06-01 to 2026-10-21, which implies request and response shapes may change. None of the 18 named call sites were reviewed or edited. The test proves that two list calls send the new header and that the method attributes exist. It does not prove that the arguments, response fields or streamed event types still match under the new version. needs-review is the right grade.

concerns.issue: The event loop (lines ~84-110) relies on event type strings such as session.thread_created, agent.thread_message_received and session.status_idle, and on fields such as event.agent_name, from_agent_name and to_agent_name. If 2026-10-21 renames any of these, the loop never hits the session.status_idle break and output is silently dropped. Nothing tests this; check it against the migration guide.

agents.create still passes default_headers anthropic-beta, multiagent={type:'coordinator', agents:[...]} and tools agent_toolset_20260401. I could not confirm these shapes are unchanged under 2026-10-21. The same applies to create_specialists.py:114 and stretch_critic_subagent.py:61/97. The test only does getattr on the methods and never calls them.

agents.retrieve/update use version=current.version and a skills list. Line ~80 calls s.get('skill_id') on current.skills items, which fails if the 1.x SDK returns typed models instead of dicts. skills.create(files=files_from_dir(...)) is only import-checked. Verify these against the SDK 1.x types.

files.list(scope_id=..., betas=[...]) and files.download(...).write_to_file are carried over unchanged (lines 39-52; also run_deal_desk.py:121-131). The test mocks an empty list, so pagination and download response handling under the new version are not exercised.

The test runs against whatever SDK is installed, so the passing check does not show that anthropic 1.0.0 itself sends 2026-10-21. Confirm the first SDK release that defaults to the new version and pin the floor to it. There is also no upper bound, so a future major could slip in.

The test tries `import httpx2 as httpx` and falls back to httpx. I could not confirm that httpx2 is what the new SDK uses. Check the SDK's dependencies, and check that http_client= accepts the client type actually installed.

checkFirst: Read the 2026-10-21 migration guide's list of code changes and map each one to the named call sites, especially managed-agents sessions/events, agents.update versioning and files.list scope_id.
Do a live dry run of setup_environment -> create_specialists -> upload_skills -> create_coordinator -> run_deal_desk against the new version and confirm the stream reaches session.status_idle.
Check the SDK 1.x types for agents.skills items (dict vs model) and for the multiagent/agents field shapes.
Confirm the minimum anthropic version that defaults to 2026-10-21 and adjust the floor in requirements.txt.

change.title: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5

tasks.reasoning:
The coordinator and critic are recorded as claude-opus-4-7, but the model string in create_specialists.py (and in any config it reads) was not captured by the scan. If it is claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 or the claude-sonnet-4-5 alias, agent creation and sessions will fail after 2026-11-30. This is uncertain. The migration agent should read the model value in create_specialists.py and any related config. If it is Sonnet 4.5, switch it to claude-sonnet-5-5 and confirm the agent config sets neither thinking disabled nor tool_choice any/tool. If it is not Sonnet 4.5, close this with no change.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-09-28-sonnet-5-5-breaking (other): Code written for Sonnet 5 can break on claude-sonnet-5-5 (thinking disabled, forced tool_choice return 400). The retirement's replacement model is claude-sonnet-5-5. Its breaking changes (thinking cannot be disabled, forced tool_choice returns 400) only matter once this task moves a model to sonnet-5-5, so the same edit must check that the agent definitions set no disabled thinking or forced tool_choice.
  Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/release-notes/api
  "Forced tool use (tool_choice types any and tool) returns a 400 error."

callSites.why: beta.agents.create sets a model, but the usage map does not record which one. Specialist agents often use a Sonnet-tier model, so this may be claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929.

No agent definition sets thinking disabled or a forced tool_choice, so the Sonnet 5.5 breaking-change item has nothing to fix.

No files changed.

The retiring model claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 is not referenced. The scan's uncertain note about create_specialists.py is resolved: its Sonnet agents use claude-sonnet-4-6, not 4.5.

> | November 30, 2026 | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations.md
